body.statement: The mechanisms in \(\text{def:informative-lock-template}\) are strictly positive and rational and induce \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{inf}}\), whose latent projections are \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}}\) and \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}=X_i-Y_i-C_i\), with \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}\in\operatorname{COPAG}_0(\{X_i,Y_i,C_i\})\), \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}\in[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}]_{\mathsf M}\), and \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}}\in[\mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}]_{\mathsf G}\). Both models therefore belong to \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{rat,bin}}^+(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}})\). Moreover \(P_{\sigma}(U_i=1\mid X_i=a)=r_a\) and \(P_{\sigma}(Y_i=1\mid X_i=a)=1/2\), while \(P(C_i=d,S_i=1\mid Y_i=b)=3/16\) for every \(b,d\in\{0,1\}\). Hence \(P_{\sigma}(X_i=a,Y_i=b,C_i=d,S_i=1)=3/64\), \(P_{\sigma}(S_i=1)=3/8\), and the two full selected observational laws assign probability \(1/8\) to every observed cell. Under \(\operatorname{do}(X_i=0)\), \(P_+(Y_i=1)=9/16\), \(P_-(Y_i=1)=7/16\), and both selection normalizers equal \(3/8\). At the root role state, \(D_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},+}}(1;0)=D_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},-}}(1;0)=1/2\), whereas \(N_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},+}}(1,1;0)=9/32\) and \(N_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},-}}(1,1;0)=7/32\), so the conditional effects are \(9/16\) and \(7/16\). The connected \(C_i\) is informative before selection because \(P(C_i=1\mid Y_i=1)=3/4\neq1/4=P(C_i=1\mid Y_i=0)\). The pair \((F_{\mathrm{inf}},F'_{\mathrm{inf}})\) consists of nested \(R_{\mathrm{inf}}\)-rooted C-forests, with \(V(F_{\mathrm{inf}})\cap\{X_i\}=\{X_i\}\), \(V(F'_{\mathrm{inf}})\cap\{X_i\}=\varnothing\), and \(R_{\mathrm{inf}}\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}},\operatorname{do}(X_i)}(\{Y_i,C_i,S_i\})\); \(D_{\max,\mathrm{inf}}=\varnothing\), so they form the terminal selected hedge for \((\{Y_i,C_i,S_i\},\{X_i\})\). Finally, replacing only \(P(S_i=1\mid Y_i=1,C_i=1)\) by \(1/2\) preserves the graph and equality of the two selected observational laws but yields denominators \(25/41\) and \(23/39\); therefore the displayed denominator equality is a tuned informative cancellation, not a structural consequence of the graph.
body.justification: The proposition instantiates the general selection-equalizer lift with informative common child and selection kernels, verifies the represented graph and terminal forest, and exhibits exact positive locked denominators with separated numerators.
body.gap: Selected hedges alone do not coordinate the conditioning denominator; this example supplies a connected exact instance and a same-graph perturbation proving that the equality is tuned rather than forced by separation.
body.consumer: The table is a positive-control certificate for rational selected-hedge synthesis and verifies the general equalizer formulas with exact arithmetic.
body.proof_tex:
All variables in \(\text{def:informative-lock-template}\) are binary.  The displayed local success probabilities and their complements belong to
\[
 \left\{\frac14,\frac12,\frac34,
              \frac5{16},\frac7{16},\frac9{16},\frac{11}{16}\right\},
\]
so every local entry is rational and strictly between zero and one, as required by \(\text{ass:rational-interior-mechanisms}\).  The table for \(X_i\) changes with \(U_i\); the table for \(Y_i\) changes with each of \(X_i\) and \(U_i\); the table for \(C_i\) changes with \(Y_i\); and the table for \(S_i\) changes with each of \(Y_i\) and \(C_i\).  Thus every displayed parent is active and the parent relations are exactly those of \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{inf}}\).

Marginalizing \(U_i\) produces the directed edge \(X_i\to Y_i\) and the bidirected edge \(X_i\leftrightarrow Y_i\) induced by \(X_i\leftarrow U_i\to Y_i\); the other displayed arrows have no latent internal vertex and remain.  Every other path has an observed internal vertex, so it creates no additional latent-projection edge.  This gives precisely \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}}\).  In the selected projection onto \(\{X_i,Y_i,C_i\}\), all three observed vertices are ancestors of \(S_i\), so the adjacent endpoint marks are tails.  The pairs \((X_i,Y_i)\) and \((Y_i,C_i)\) are adjacent.  The remaining pair is nonadjacent: in the ancestral moral graph for \(\{X_i,C_i,Y_i,S_i\}\), after conditioning on and removing \(Y_i,S_i\), the vertex \(C_i\) is disconnected from the component containing \(X_i\).  Hence
\[
 \mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}=X_i-Y_i-C_i.                 \tag{7}
\]
The three-node noncollider chain has no invariant endpoint mark in its input-free equivalence class.  Its completed partial graph is therefore
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}
 =X_i\mathbin{\circ\!-\!\circ}Y_i
       \mathbin{\circ\!-\!\circ}C_i,
\]
and the direct projection checks give
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}\in\operatorname{COPAG}_0(\{X_i,Y_i,C_i\}),
 \quad \mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}\in[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}]_{\mathsf M},
 \quad \mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}}\in[\mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}]_{\mathsf G}. \tag{8}
\]
Together with binary support from \(\text{ass:binary-certificate-support}\), positivity and rationality, (8) and \(\text{def:rational-binary-class}\) imply
\[
 \mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},+},\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},-}
 \in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{rat,bin}}^+(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}). \tag{9}
\]

We next compute the unselected base laws.  Since \(P(U_i=1)=1/2\), Bayes' rule, with the positive denominators displayed below, gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P(X_i=1)&=\tfrac12\tfrac14+\tfrac12\tfrac34=\tfrac12,&
 P(U_i=1\mid X_i=1)&=\frac{(1/2)(3/4)}{1/2}=\tfrac34=r_1,\\
 P(X_i=0)&=\tfrac12\tfrac34+\tfrac12\tfrac14=\tfrac12,&
 P(U_i=1\mid X_i=0)&=\frac{(1/2)(1/4)}{1/2}=\tfrac14=r_0.
\end{aligned}                                                     \tag{10}
\]
For \(a\in\{0,1\}\), iterated expectation and the outcome table in \(\text{def:informative-lock-template}\) therefore yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_\sigma(Y_i=1\mid X_i=a)
 &=\sum_{u=0}^1
   \left\{\frac12+\frac{\sigma}{4}(u-r_a)\right\}
   P(U_i=u\mid X_i=a)\\
 &=\frac12+\frac{\sigma}{4}
   \{P(U_i=1\mid X_i=a)-r_a\}=\frac12.                 \tag{11}
\end{aligned}
\]
Equations (10)--(11) show that both signs have the same base observational law, with
\[
 P_\sigma(X_i=a,Y_i=b)=\frac14
 \quad\text{for every }a,b\in\{0,1\}.                  \tag{12}
\]
Under \(\operatorname{do}(X_i=0)\), modularity deletes the factor for \(X_i\) but leaves \(U_i\) fair.  Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_+(Y_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))
 &=\frac12+\frac14\left(\frac12-\frac14\right)=\frac9{16},\\
 P_-(Y_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))
 &=\frac12-\frac14\left(\frac12-\frac14\right)=\frac7{16}. \tag{13}
\end{aligned}
\]

The appended tables are the concrete instance of \(\text{lem:selection-equalizer-lift}\) with
\[
 g_b(d):=P(C_i=d\mid Y_i=b),
 \qquad \lambda_0=\lambda_1:=\frac3{16},
 \qquad \Lambda=\frac38.                                \tag{14}
\]
Indeed, for every \(b,d\in\{0,1\}\), direct multiplication gives
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
 (b,d)&(0,0)&(0,1)&(1,0)&(1,1)\\ \hline
 g_b(d)P(S_i=1\mid Y_i=b,C_i=d)
 &(3/4)(1/4)&(1/4)(3/4)&(1/4)(3/4)&(3/4)(1/4)
\end{array}
=\frac3{16}.                                             \tag{15}
\]
Moreover \(0<3/16<1/4=\min_b g_b(d)\).  Both new parent relations are active, as already checked before (7), so the graph qualification of the equalizer lemma is also satisfied.  Applying its observational identity to (12) gives
\[
 P_\sigma(X_i=a,Y_i=b,C_i=d,S_i=1)
 =\frac14\frac3{16}=\frac3{64}.                         \tag{16}
\]
Summing (16) over the eight observed cells gives \(P_\sigma(S_i=1)=3/8\); dividing by this positive normalizer gives
\[
 P_\sigma(X_i=a,Y_i=b,C_i=d\mid S_i=1)
 =\frac{3/64}{3/8}=\frac18.                              \tag{17}
\]
Thus the two full selected observational laws agree and have full support.

The interventional identities of \(\text{lem:selection-equalizer-lift}\), (13), and (14) give both selection normalizers as \(3/8\) and give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 D_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},\sigma}}(1;0)
 &=\frac{\lambda_1}{\Lambda}=\frac12,\\
 N_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},+}}(1,1;0)
 &=\frac9{16}\frac{\lambda_1}{\Lambda}=\frac9{32},\\
 N_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},-}}(1,1;0)
 &=\frac7{16}\frac{\lambda_1}{\Lambda}=\frac7{32}.    \tag{18}
\end{aligned}
\]
The common denominator in (18) is positive, so division gives selected conditional effects \(9/16\) and \(7/16\).  Directly from the common \(C_i\) table,
\[
 P(C_i=1\mid Y_i=1)=\frac34\ne\frac14
 =P(C_i=1\mid Y_i=0),                                   \tag{19}
\]
which proves that the connected conditioning coordinate is informative before selection.

For the graphical obstruction, \(F_{\mathrm{inf}}\) is bidirected-connected, every vertex has at most one directed child, and its unique childless root is \(Y_i\).  The singleton \(F'_{\mathrm{inf}}\) is a proper C-subforest with the same root.  Directly,
\[
 V(F_{\mathrm{inf}})\cap\{X_i\}=\{X_i\},
 \qquad
 V(F'_{\mathrm{inf}})\cap\{X_i\}=\varnothing.          \tag{20}
\]
After intervention on \(X_i\), the root \(Y_i\) remains an ancestor of the terminal set: it belongs to that set and has directed paths to \(C_i\) and \(S_i\).  Hence
\[
 R_{\mathrm{inf}}=\{Y_i\}
 \subseteq\operatorname{An}_{\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}},\operatorname{do}(X_i)}
 (\{Y_i,C_i,S_i\}).                                     \tag{21}
\]
It remains to verify the maximal selection-exchange coordinate rather than infer it from the absence of an input vertex in the original graph.  Since \(S=\{S_i\}\), the only nonempty candidate is \(D=\{S_i\}\).  In the corresponding input-augmented graph, the length-two path
\[
 I_{S_i}\longrightarrow S_i\longleftarrow C_i           \tag{22}
\]
is open when conditioning on \(S_i\): its sole internal vertex is a conditioned collider, and there is no noncollider on the path that could block it.  Thus \(I_{S_i}\) and \(C_i\) fail the required id-separation, so \(\{S_i\}\) is inadmissible.  The empty set is admissible vacuously and is the only remaining subset; consequently its unique maximal value is
\[
 D_{\max,\mathrm{inf}}=\varnothing.                     \tag{23}
\]
The bidirected-connectivity, common-root, treatment-intersection, ancestry, and maximal-exchange checks (20)--(23) are the terminal selected-hedge predicates in \(\text{def:informative-graph-certificate}\).  Therefore \((F_{\mathrm{inf}},F'_{\mathrm{inf}})\) is the asserted terminal selected hedge.

Finally, form \(\widetilde P\) by changing only
\(P(S_i=1\mid Y_i=1,C_i=1)\) from \(1/4\) to \(1/2\).  The new entry and its complement are positive rational numbers.  At fixed \(C_i=0\), the selection table still changes with \(Y_i\), and at fixed \(Y_i=0\), it still changes with \(C_i\); hence both arrows into \(S_i\) remain active and the represented graph is unchanged.  Equations (10)--(12) are unchanged, so the two signs still have the same unselected observed law.  Because their \(C_i\) and modified \(S_i\) kernels are also common, factorization gives identical selected observational masses, and therefore identical full selected observational laws, for the two signs.

Put \(p=P_\sigma(Y_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))\).  For \(Y_i=0\), summing the unchanged products in (15) gives \(P(S_i=1\mid Y_i=0)=3/8\).  For \(Y_i=1\), the \(C_i=0\) product remains \(3/16\), while the modified \(C_i=1\) product is \((3/4)(1/2)=3/8\); hence \(P(S_i=1\mid Y_i=1)=9/16\).  It follows that
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widetilde P(S_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))
 &=(1-p)\frac38+p\frac9{16}=\frac{6+3p}{16},\\
 \widetilde P(C_i=1,S_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))
 &=(1-p)\frac3{16}+p\frac38=\frac{3+3p}{16}.            \tag{24}
\end{aligned}
\]
The first quantity in (24) is positive.  Therefore the modified selected denominator is
\[
 \widetilde D_\sigma(1;0)
 =\frac{3+3p}{6+3p}=\frac{1+p}{2+p}.                    \tag{25}
\]
Substitution of \(p=9/16\) and \(p=7/16\) from (13) yields
\[
 \widetilde D_+=\frac{25}{41},
 \qquad
 \widetilde D_-=\frac{23}{39},                         \tag{26}
\]
and these fractions are unequal because \(25\cdot39=975\ne943=23\cdot41\).  Thus the denominator equality in (18) is the tuned informative cancellation furnished by (14)--(15), not a consequence of the represented graph.
